metadata.description: how this line's cuneiform was laid out per sign: 0 not aligned, 1 counts matched and were zipped, 2 aligned after absorbing surplus U+2592 placeholders into a recorded lacuna, 3 aligned after expanding a compound logogram, 4 aligned using the derived numeral rule. Higher numbers are weaker evidence, so a query wanting only the safest material filters cu_aligned=1. Measured against the learned reading->sign table, level 1 assignments contradict it in 0.01% of cases, level 2 in 0.96% and level 3 in 0.15%; see reports/alignment.md. Level 4 no longer occurs -- the numerals are now learned spellings and reach level 3 -- but the value is kept so an older dataset still reads correctly.

metadata.description: 1 where the edition printed `?°?` for this sign -- a sign it could not draw. The sign is on the tablet and occupies its slot; only the glyph is missing, so `cu_sign` is absent here for a reason that is a fact about the source, not a limit of the alignment. Set on the 2,347 such signs whose line aligned; `cu` holds 7,462 marks in all, the other 5,115 on the 3,601 lines that align at level 0 and so carry no per-sign values at all. What fails to render is a recognisable class: ad-hoc indices (`dan_x`), an unnormalised ASCII `h` for the corpus's `h-breve` (`ha`, `hu`), a Glossenkeil left in SimTex input form (`:ku`), and editorial text in the sign stream (`leer`, `erasure`).
